LC 56 0296
To amend Chapter 12 of Title 50 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, relating to
commissions and other agencies, so as to create the Georgia Interagency Council for the
Homeless; to provide for the purpose, membership, and duties of such council; to provide for
reporting of activities; to provide for compensation; to provide for legislative findings; to
provide for related matters; to repeal conflicting laws; and for other purposes.
BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF GEORGIA:
SECTION 1.
The General Assembly finds that:
(1) Every Georgian has the right to life, liberty, and property under the Constitution of the
State of Georgia;
(2) The protection of persons and property is the paramount duty of government;
(3) No Georgian shall be denied equal protection under the law;
(4) The government of the State of Georgia is instituted for the protection, security, and
benefit of the people;
(5) In 2022, the Georgia State Senate created a Study Committee on Unsheltered
Homelessness to study the issue, assess evidence for different policies, solicit input, and
LC 56 0296
develop recommendations for improvements to the law that would aid those experiencing
homelessness;
(6) In 2022, the Georgia State Senate found that the state should continue to oppose the
criminalization of homelessness, and the Study Committee on Unsheltered Homelessness
did not recommend any legal action against unsheltered or sheltered homeless individuals
based on housing status; and
(7) This Act reinforces the General Assembly's commitment to the safety and security of
those state residents who remain unhoused.
SECTION 2.
Chapter 12 of Title 50 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, relating to commissions
and other agencies, is amended by adding a new article to read as follows:
"ARTICLE 9
50-12-140.
(a) There is created the Georgia Interagency Council for the Homeless for the purpose of
ensuring a coordinated state-wide approach to addressing homelessness.
(b) As used in this Code section, the term 'council' means the Georgia Interagency Council
for the Homeless.
(c) The council shall consist of the following 21 members who shall be appointed to serve
at the pleasure of the Governor:
(1) The commissioner of community affairs or his or her designee;
(2) One member from the Attorney General's office;
(3) One member from the Department of Behavioral Health and Developmental
Disabilities;
(4) One member from the Department of Corrections;
LC 56 0296
(5) One member from the Division of Aging Services within the Department of Human
Services;
(6) One member from the Governor's Office for Children and Families;
(7) One member from the Department of Veterans Service;
(8) One member from the Georgia Housing and Finance Authority;
(9) One member from the Department of Community Affairs;
(10) One member from the Department of Transportation;
(11) One member from the Department of Public Health;
(12) One member from the Department of Public Safety;
(13) One member from the State Board of Pardons and Paroles;
(14) One member from the Continuum of Care Network;
(15) One member from the Department of Community Supervision;
(16) Three members who have personally experienced homelessness; and
(17) Three members representing service providers to the homeless.
(d) Councilmembers appointed pursuant to paragraphs (14) and (15) of subsection (c) of
this Code section shall serve for a period of three years.
(e) A vacancy on the council shall be filled in the same manner as the original appointment
was made.
(f) The commissioner of community affairs or his or her appointee shall serve as the
chairperson of the council.
(g) The council shall:
(1) Survey current resources for services for the homeless in this state;
(2) Initiate an evaluation of the current and future needs for the services;
(3) Assist in coordinating and providing state-wide services for all homeless individuals
in this state;
(4)   Increase the flow of information among separate providers and appropriate
authorities;
LC 56 0296
(5) Develop guidelines to monitor the provision of services for the homeless and the
methods of delivering those services;
(6) Coordinate with the State Workforce Development Board, homeless shelters, and
public and private entities to provide homeless individuals information on services
available to assist them in obtaining employment and job training;
(7) Establish a central resource and information center for the homeless in this state;
(8) Coordinate state-wide efforts to combat the criminalization of homelessness;
(9) Ensure that local or state-wide nonprofit organizations perform the duties under this
subsection that the council is unable to perform; and
(10) Meet at least once per quarter to set the goals of the council and review the work
described in this Code section.
(h) The council, no later than October 1, 2025, and annually thereafter, shall submit to the
office of the Governor a report detailing the council's activities, findings, and any
recommendations. Any reports generated by the council shall be made available on an
annual basis by the department to the members of the General Assembly, all departments
and agencies of state government, all county and municipal governments, and members of
the general public by posting such reports on the appropriate state agency public websites.
(i) Councilmembers shall receive no compensation for their services but shall be allowed
actual and necessary expenses in the performance of their duties. Citizen members shall
receive a daily expense allowance in the amount specified in subsection (b) of Code
Section 45-7-21 as well as the mileage or transportation allowance authorized for state
employees. If any members selected to serve on the council are state officials or are state
employees, they shall receive no compensation for their services on the council but shall
be reimbursed for expenses incurred in the performance of their duties as members of the
council in the same manner as reimbursements are made in their capacity as state officials
or state employees. The funds necessary for the reimbursement of the expenses of state
LC 56 0296
officials and state employees shall come from funds appropriated to or otherwise available
to their respective departments."
SECTION 3.
All laws and parts of laws in conflict with this Act are repealed.

SB 170/AP
To amend Chapter 2 of Title 31 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, relating to the
Department of Community Health, so as to provide for a grant program for the purpose of
providing funding to certain rural hospitals for acquiring or installing backup generators to
ensure continuity of operation during a state of emergency; to provide that the department
shall consult with the Georgia Emergency Management and Homeland Security Agency in
establishing grant criteria; to provide for the department to establish grant amounts; to
provide for definitions; to provide for related matters; to provide for an effective date; to
repeal conflicting laws; and for other purposes.
BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF GEORGIA:
SECTION 1.
Chapter 2 of Title 31 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, relating to the Department
of Community Health, is amended by adding a new Code section to read as follows:
"31-2-20.
(a) As used in this Code section, the term:
SB 170/AP
(1) 'Affected rural hospital' means a non-profit or not for profit acute care hospital
located in a rural county that contains fewer than 100 beds and is located in any region
of the state in which the Governor declared a state of emergency after July 1, 2024.
(2) 'Rural county' means a county in this state that has a population of less than 50,000
according to the United States decennial census of 2020 or any future such census;
provided, however, that for counties which contain a military base or installation, the
military personnel and their dependents living in such county shall be excluded from the
total population of such county for purposes of this definition.
(b) Subject to appropriations by the General Assembly or other available funding,
including, but not limited to, federal funding, the department shall establish a grant
program to provide funding to affected rural hospitals for the purpose of acquiring,
installing, or both acquiring and installing backup generators to ensure continuity of
operation during a state of emergency. The department, in consultation with the director
of emergency management and homeland security shall establish grant criteria and make
award decisions; provided, however, that the department and the director of emergency
management and homeland security shall only provide funding to those affected rural
hospitals that do not have a backup generator as of the effective date of this Act and have
not received any federal assistance for the purpose of acquiring or installing a backup
generator. The department shall be authorized to establish the grant amount awarded to
each recipient on a case-by-case basis."
SECTION 2.
This Act shall become effective upon its approval by the Governor or upon its becoming law
without such approval.
SECTION 3.
All laws and parts of laws in conflict with this Act are repealed.

LC 44 3197S
To amend Chapter 2 of Title 31 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, relating to the
Department of Community Health, so as to provide for a grant program for the purpose of
providing funding to certain rural hospitals for acquiring or installing backup generators to
ensure continuity of operation during a state of emergency; to provide that the department
shall consult with the Georgia Emergency Management and Homeland Security Agency in
establishing grant criteria; to provide for the department to establish grant amounts; to
provide for definitions; to provide for related matters; to provide for an effective date; to
repeal conflicting laws; and for other purposes.
BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF GEORGIA:
SECTION 1.
Chapter 2 of Title 31 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, relating to the Department
of Community Health, is amended by adding a new Code section to read as follows:
"31-2-20.
(a) As used in this Code section, the term:
LC 44 3197S
(1) 'Affected rural hospital' means an acute care hospital located in a rural county that
contains fewer than 100 beds and is located in any region of the state in which the
Governor declared a state of emergency after July 1, 2024.
(2) 'Rural county' means a county in this state that has a population of less than 50,000
according to the United States decennial census of 2020 or any future such census;
provided, however, that for counties which contain a military base or installation, the
military personnel and their dependents living in such county shall be excluded from the
total population of such county for purposes of this definition.
(b) Subject to appropriations by the General Assembly or other available funding, the
department shall establish a grant program to provide funding to affected rural hospitals
for the purpose of acquiring, installing, or both acquiring and installing backup generators
to ensure continuity of operation during a state of emergency. The department, in
consultation with the director of emergency management and homeland security shall
establish grant criteria and make award decisions; provided, however, that the department
and the director of emergency management and homeland security shall, to the greatest
extent possible, prioritize the approval of applications of those affected rural hospitals
lacking backup generators and the means by which to install them. The department shall
be authorized to establish the grant amount awarded to each recipient on a case-by-case
basis."
SECTION 2.
This Act shall become effective upon its approval by the Governor or upon its becoming law
without such approval.
SECTION 3.
All laws and parts of laws in conflict with this Act are repealed.
